human_rationale: Public-style quickstart; all credential strings are placeholders or documented examples, not live secrets.
The invoice contains full routing and bank account numbers, which meet Financial / PCI and its Highly Confidential floor.
The health outcomes are aggregated and explicitly contain no identifiers, so PHI does not apply; no public-release intent is stated.
This is a blank employee form. Empty fields are specifically excluded from PII and contain no actual financial data.
Complete payment-card numbers appear in the chargeback record, clearly meeting Financial / PCI.
The notebook describes a novel unpublished method and results and mentions protecting the work before presentation, meeting Intellectual Property.
The file contains operational Python logic and an internal host, which reasonably fits non-public Source Code.
The trace exposes a complete live-looking bearer token, which meets Credentials / Secrets.
The contract contains non-public multi-million-dollar commercial terms whose disclosure could harm the organization, but no named category clearly applies.
The document explicitly describes aggregated, non-identifiable health outcomes, so PHI does not apply and Internal is the default.
The clinic statistics are aggregated and explicitly de-identified; without public-release intent, Internal is appropriate.
A named patient and MRN are linked to medication and diagnosis, clearly meeting PHI.
The careers FAQ targets external applicants and points to a public careers page, establishing public-release intent.
Routine Facilities meeting notes contain ordinary internal operational information and no defined sensitive category.
Private divorce and immigration circumstances are tied to a named employee, directly meeting the PII definition.
The file is explicitly internal code. It reads a key from an environment variable rather than containing the secret, so only Source Code applies.
This recruiting advertisement directs applicants to a public careers page and is clearly intended for public distribution.
The employee data sheet is a blank template; empty personal and bank fields do not constitute actual PII or financial data.
The postmortem reveals internal hosts, outage impact and operational weaknesses, making external disclosure plausibly harmful, though no named category clearly applies.
The hiring notice explicitly directs applicants to a public careers page, indicating public-release intent.
This is a historical completed-merger case rather than non-public future strategy. Public status is not explicit, so Internal is the default.
The customer story is awaiting customer approval and is therefore not yet approved for public release; the non-public customer results make Confidential defensible.
Only business names, titles, departments, work emails and offices are listed; business contact details alone are explicitly excluded from PII.
Usernames and password hashes are sensitive security information, but hashes are not clearly live passwords, keys or tokens under the Credentials / Secrets definition.
The draft talk discusses a non-public technical approach and measured results before presentation, fitting unpublished technical Intellectual Property.
The unsubmitted manuscript describes a novel method and unpublished research results, directly matching Intellectual Property.
These non-public board minutes discuss competitive landscape and priorities, but the excerpt lacks a concrete strategic plan; Confidential is defensible.
Internal compensation bands are restricted sensitive business information, although they do not clearly meet a named data category.
